title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Confirmatory Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered, confirmatory experiment that evaluates template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating in an LLM-driven network-configuration pipeline under adversarially crafted intents. The preregistered formal estimand was the paired difference in per-intent acceptance-for-deployment as determined by a deterministic validator (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). We executed the frozen plan on 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes=300; completed episodes=282; complete_pairs_included=141) using a single model (gpt-5-mini) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Observed outcomes on complete pairs: baseline accepted 135/141 (95.7447%), guarded accepted 141/141 (100.0%); paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165; exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Crucially, outcome semantics used in execution define a "success" as acceptance-for-deployment by the validator (i.e., a validator-deemed valid configuration). We clarify a preregistration ambiguity: natural-language H1 described reducing attack/unsafe-acceptance, but the preregistered formal estimand and the executed analysis measured acceptance-for-deployment (validator-valid outputs). Under that formal estimand, the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable increase in validator-accepted configurations; exploratory traces show this improvement stems from sanitizer/repair activity that corrected inputs or candidates rejected under baseline. The study is limited to synthetic intent templates, a single model, and a single deterministic validator; the preregistered benign-control (M=50) and related false-positive-blocking secondary estimands were not executed and are reported as unperformed preregistered items. All execution artifacts and analysis files are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: LLMs hold promise for reducing operator effort by translating high-level intent to device configuration, but they also produce safety- and correctness-critical failures (hallucination, malformed CLI, semantic violations, prompt injection) that risk operational impact. Prior work suggests that pairing generative models with deterministic verifiers and localized repair reduces some error classes [1],[2],[3]. We study a narrowly scoped, preregistered research question: how effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating at preventing adversarially crafted intents from producing unsafe or policy-violating network configurations in an LLM-driven NetOps pipeline? Contributions. (1) A preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) with a formal paired estimand measuring acceptance-for-deployment by a deterministic validator. (2) A deterministic, artifact-backed analysis showing a small but statistically detectable change in per-intent acceptance between a baseline (LLM-only) and a guarded pipeline (sanitization + verifier-gating + optional automated repair) on synthetic adversarial intents. (3) A concise reconciliation of a preregistration ambiguity about outcome semantics, explicit disclosure of unperformed preregistered items, and a failure-analysis discussion grounded in archived traces.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification frameworks (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide rapid checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and are natural validators for generate–validate pipelines [1],[2]. Recent NetOps work demonstrates that LLMs produce promising drafts but commit syntax, topology, and semantic errors; augmenting generation with verifier feedback or repair improves outcomes in prototype tasks [3]. Surveys and benchmarks for LLMs in NetOps/AIOps highlight fragmented evaluation practices and call for operationally meaningful metrics beyond text match [4],[5]. Security studies document prompt-injection and indirect attacks against LLM-integrated applications, motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses in operational pipelines [6]. Tool-augmented LM research (e.g., Toolformer) shows practical value from orchestrating external checks during generation [7]. The present study situates itself in the generate–validate–repair literature and focuses on the operational impact of deterministic gating under a constrained adversary model.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and formal estimand. We preregistered study cand-2026-03 before observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The formal primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where the binary per-intent outcome equals 1 if the pipeline variant would accept a configuration for deployment as judged by the deterministic validator (validator-valid = accepted). Note and reconciliation: the preregistration text included a natural-language H1 phrased as a reduction in attack/unsafe acceptance; the registered formal estimand and the executed analysis measured validator acceptance-for-deployment. We therefore interpret results with respect to the formal estimand and explicitly disclose the natural-language ambiguity. Design and interventions. Confirmatory paired design on adversarial intents: N=150 adversarial intents (planned episodes=300). Conditions: Baseline = single-shot LLM generation (gpt-5-mini) scored by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Guarded = template-based input sanitization followed by LLM generation; the validator blocks any candidate failing safety checks (verifier-gating). The preregistration allowed at most one automated repair call per run under a frozen repair policy. Execution and instrumentation. Models and tools used exactly as recorded: model declared as gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) and validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The task bank was generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 using synthetic intent templates covering interface admin, MTU, VLAN, static routes, and safe-change workflow constraints. Generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate (the same initial candidate was produced in the shared_initial_generation stage and reused across conditions where applicable). The model configuration archived shows temperature explicitly set to null/unset (execution/model_configuration.json); we report this literal setting and do not infer provider-internal default sampling behavior. Recording and missingness. Planned runs=300; completed episodes=282; failed episodes=18; complete_pairs included in primary analysis=141. Technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, parser error) were logged and handled per the preregistered missingness plan: pairs were excluded only when both paired runs were technical failures (both-missing pairs = 9). Provider-call and stage counts (shared_initial_generation and repair counts) are recorded in the archived provider-call audit and deterministic reconciliation artifacts and are cited for implementation detail.
sections.results: Execution summary and counts. Planned episodes=300; completed episodes=282; failed episodes=18; model_calls_used=156. Primary confirmatory analysis used the 141 complete pairs (pairs where at least one run produced a scorable result). Observed per-pair acceptance outcomes (complete_pairs=141): baseline_successes = 135 (135/141 = 0.9574468085106383); guarded_successes = 141 (141/141 = 1.0). Contingency counts (from the archived paired_contingency_table): n11 (both accepted) = 135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 6; n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1) = 0; n00 = 0. Statistical inference. We applied the preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test on paired outcomes: p = 0.03125. The point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. Interpretation aligned to the formal estimand. Because the executed binary outcome equals validator-accepted-for-deployment, the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable increase in the rate of validator-accepted configurations on the included pairs. This improvement does not mean the guarded pipeline made the generator "safer" in the sense of rejecting unsafe attacker-induced outputs; instead, archived validator traces and provider-call logs indicate that sanitizer or repair activity corrected or permitted candidate configurations that the baseline path had caused to be rejected (the six discordant n10 pairs correspond to cases where guarded runs applied repair/sanitization enabling acceptance where the baseline lacked such correction). Missingness and sensitivity. Both-missing pairs = 9 (18 failed episodes total). Sensitivity analyses (archive) treat missing generative outputs as failures and widen CIs; those analyses do not overturn the primary qualitative direction but reduce precision. Unperformed preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control set (M=50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed and are therefore reported as unperformed preregistered items; they appear in the preregistration but are absent from execution artifacts.
sections.discussion: Reconciliation of preregistration language. A reviewer correctly noted a semantic inconsistency between the preregistered natural-language H1 (framed as reducing attack/unsafe-acceptance) and the formal estimand executed here. We resolve that by (i) reporting the formal estimand executed (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) and its explicit outcome semantics (validator-accepted-for-deployment = success), and (ii) reframing claims to match the archived analysis. Under that formal estimand, the guarded pipeline increased validator acceptance by ≈4.25 percentage points on included pairs (p=0.03125). Operational interpretation. In this constrained synthetic setting, combining input sanitization with deterministic verifier-gating plus limited automated repair reduced baseline rejections of validator-valid configurations (i.e., repaired or corrected candidate paths were accepted under guarded but rejected under baseline). This behavior has two operational implications: (a) well-scoped sanitization and repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that a naive baseline generation might fail to produce; (b) gating remains necessary but must be carefully specified because a gate that only blocks can increase false negatives unless paired with repair or corrective sanitization. Threats to validity. Construct validity: the validator encodes a limited set of safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants) and does not represent full protocol semantics or live runtime state. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic intents, and a single validator implementation limit generalization to multi-vendor, protocol-diverse production networks. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective N; exclusion rules were preregistered and applied (both-run failures excluded). Security coverage: the adversary model was limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection and indirect attacks in richer retrieval-augmented pipelines remain open. Recommendations. Practitioners should (1) pair LLM generators with deterministic validators and well-tested repair routines, (2) expand validator coverage toward protocol-level and multi-vendor semantics before trustful deployment, and (3) treat gating policies and repair policies jointly to avoid excessive false negatives.
sections.conclusion: We present a preregistered, confirmatory evaluation showing that, under the preregistered formal estimand (validator-accepted-for-deployment), a guarded pipeline (input sanitization + deterministic verifier-gating + limited repair) produced a small but statistically detectable increase in validator-accepted configurations on a synthetic adversarial intent bank (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p=0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). We explicitly reconcile a preregistration ambiguity: natural-language H1 discussed reducing attack/unsafe-acceptance but the executed formal estimand measured acceptance-for-deployment. Important limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, validator scope, and unperformed benign-control runs) constrain external claims. Future work should expand validator semantics, diversify models and vendors, execute the preregistered benign-control and false-positive-blocking analyses, and evaluate defenses against broader prompt-injection vectors. Archived execution artifacts and analysis files support the numeric claims reported here.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; all literature review, study selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Models and tools (declared): primary generator = gpt-5-mini (provider field recorded as openai_responses), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Execution accounting (archived): planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; complete_pairs used in primary analysis = 141; model_calls_used = 156. Outcome semantics: the preregistered formal estimand executed is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a per-intent binary "success" equals acceptance-for-deployment by the deterministic validator (validator-valid = accepted). Note: a natural-language H1 in the preregistration described reducing attack/unsafe acceptance; we explicitly reconcile that ambiguity in the manuscript and report results against the preregistered formal estimand. Unperformed preregistered items: the preregistered benign-control set (M = 50) and the associated false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed and are reported as unperformed preregistered items. Implementation specifics archived: the model configuration records temperature = null/unset (see archived execution/model_configuration.json); generation semantics were implemented with a shared_initial_generation stage (shared_initial_candidate) and a preregistered single-repair-call allowance; provider-call audits and stage counts (shared_initial_generation and repair counts) are recorded in the archived provider-call audit and deterministic reconciliation artifacts. Missingness handling: pairs were excluded only when both paired runs were technical failures per the preregistered missingness plan (both-missing pairs = 9). Reproducibility and provenance: the exact initial prompting strategy, tool-call traces, model responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript materials; readers should consult the archived bundle for full manifests and machine-verifiable artifacts. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.

A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; we report and interpret results with respect to the archived formal estimand and explicitly disclose the phrasing ambiguity.
